blocks.text: The project `.env` only feeds `${VAR}` interpolation in the Compose file; `env_file:` and `environment:` are what put variables into containers.

blocks.code:
services:
  db:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:${POSTGRES_TAG:-pg17}
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?DB_PASSWORD is required}
  api:
    env_file: [./config/api.env]

items: `${VAR:-d}` default if unset or empty; `${VAR-d}` only if unset.

blocks.text: Classic bugs: the variable is in .env but missing in the container; a shell-exported var silently overrides .env; a healthcheck's `$POSTGRES_USER` gets interpolated empty on the host. Check `docker compose config`.

Q: "DB_PASSWORD is in .env but the container doesn't have it. Why?" A: ".env is only used for interpolating the Compose file. It reaches a container only if referenced in environment: (e.g., DB_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}) or loaded via env_file:."
